entities.summary:
The Battle of Maritsa, fought on September 26, 1371, near the village of Chernomen, was a pivotal event in the decline of the Byzantine Empire. The battle saw the forces of the Ottoman Empire under the command of Murad I defeat a combined force of Bulgarian, Serbian, and Byzantine troops led by the Emperor John V Palaiologos. The decisive victory of the Ottomans marked the beginning of their expansion into the Balkans and the eventual fall of Constantinople in 1453.

The Battle of Maritsa was a turning point in the history of the region, as it led to the Ottoman Empire's consolidation of power in the Balkans and their subsequent expansion into Europe. The battle also marked the beginning of the end of the Byzantine Empire, which would eventually fall to the Ottomans in 1453.

The consequences of the Battle of Maritsa can still be felt today, as the Ottoman Empire's expansion into the Balkans and Europe had a profound impact on the region's politics, culture, and history. The battle also marked the beginning of the Ottoman Empire's long and complex relationship with the West, which would continue to shape the course of international relations for centuries to come.

As the Byzantine historian Theodore Spandounes wrote, 'The fall of the Empire of the Romans was a calamity, a calamity that lasted for centuries, and it was the cause of many evils.'
